subject: Cloud Computing
title: Spotify Streams from the Cloud
description: A fast breakdown of Spotify Streams from the Cloud for builders.

hook.text: Spotify serves 100 million songs to 600 million users. Not one song lives on your phone.

buildup.text: Every time you press play, Spotify fetches the track from Google Cloud's servers worldwide.

discovery.text: Spotify moved from its own data centers to Google Cloud in 2016 for global scale.

twist.text: Streaming only works because cloud data centers sit close enough for zero-lag audio playback.

climax.text: Cloud computing turned music from a product you buy into a service you stream.

punchline.text: You don't own music anymore. You rent it from the cloud.

quiz.question: Which cloud provider does Spotify primarily use?

details.summary: Spotify migrated from its own data centers to Google Cloud Platform, completing the move in 2018. The migration improved their ability to scale globally, reduced operational overhead, and allowed engineering teams to focus on music features rather than infrastructure management.
details.whyItMatters: Spotify's migration to GCP showed that even companies with their own data centers benefit from cloud flexibility. It also validated GCP as a serious competitor to AWS for large-scale workloads.
takeaways: Spotify migrated from owned data centers to Google Cloud
The move reduced operational burden on engineering teams
It validated GCP for demanding real-time streaming workloads

faq.question: Why did Spotify choose Google Cloud?
faq.answer: Spotify valued Google's strengths in data analytics, machine learning, and BigQuery for their recommendation engine. Google's global network offered low-latency streaming worldwide. The partnership also gave Spotify access to Google's Kubernetes expertise for their containerized architecture.

faq.question: How long did the migration take?
faq.answer: The full migration took about two years. Spotify used a gradual approach, moving services incrementally while maintaining service quality. They developed internal tools for migration management and ran workloads in both environments during the transition period.
